title: Complete Chinese Xia/Shang/Zhou King Lists (Legge Bamboo Books), Nihongi Vol. I Kami & 25 Emperors (Aston), & Complete Secret History of the Mongols Borjigin Genealogy (Rachewiltz)

nodes.name: Complete Xia Dynasty (All 17 Kings, Bamboo Books): Yu → Qi → Tai Kang → Zhong Kang → Xiang → Shao Kang → Zhu → Huai → Mang → Xie → Bu Jiang → Jiong → Jin → Kong Jia → Gao → Fa → Jie
nodes.era: c. 1989-1557 BCE (Bamboo Books Part III; Shoo King)
nodes.role: First Hereditary Dynasty of China (17 Kings, 432-471 yrs)
sources: Legge Chinese Classics Vol. III (Proleg. pp. 117-127; Shoo pp. 160-171)
nodes.notes: Complete father-son & brother succession from Yu the Great (son of Gun) through the usurpation of Hou Yi & Han Zhuo, restoration by posthumous son Shao Kang (+ Empress Min), 59-yr reign of Bu Jiang, and final tyrant Jie (overthrown by Tang of Shang).

nodes.name: Complete Shang / Yin Dynasty (All 30 Kings, Bamboo Books): Tang → Tai Jia → Tai Wu → Zu Yi → Pan Geng → Wu Ding → Zu Jia → Wen Ding → Di Yi → Di Xin (King Zhou)
nodes.era: c. 1557-1049 BCE (Bamboo Books Part IV; Shoo King)
nodes.role: Oracle-Bone Bronze Age Dynasty (30 Kings Including Tang, Pan Geng & Wu Ding)
sources: Legge Chinese Classics Vol. III (Proleg. pp. 128-141; Shoo pp. 193-278)
nodes.notes: Descended from Emperor Ku & Jiandi -> Xie (13 generations to Tang the Victorious). Features lateral brother-to-brother succession (e.g., 4 brothers Yang Jia -> Pan Geng -> Xiao Xin -> Xiao Yi!), Pan Geng's move to Yin, Wu Ding's 59-yr golden age, and Di Xin's fall at Muye to King Wu of Zhou.

nodes.name: Complete Zhou Dynasty (All 34 Kings, Bamboo Books): Pre-Dynastic (Hou Ji → Danfu → King Wen) → 12 Western Zhou (King Wu → Cheng → Kang → Mu → Li → Xuan → You) → 22 Eastern Zhou (King Ping → King Nan)
nodes.era: 1049-256 BCE (Bamboo Books Part V, Proleg. pp. 142-183)
nodes.role: Longest Dynasty in Chinese History (Mandate of Heaven, Spring & Autumn, Warring States)
sources: Legge Chinese Classics Vol. III (Proleg. pp. 142-183)
nodes.notes: From Emperor Ku & Jiang Yuan -> Hou Ji -> Gong Liu -> Old Duke Danfu (King Tai) -> Jili -> King Wen -> King Wu & Duke of Zhou -> 12 Western Zhou kings (ending when King You fell in 771 BCE) -> 22 Eastern Zhou kings at Luoyang (Ping through King Nan, era of Confucius & Laozi!).

nodes.name: Imperial China Dynastic Bridges: Han Dynasty (Liu Bang / Gaozu → Emperor Wu / Han Wudi; Sima Qian) & Tang Dynasty (Li Yuan → Taizong → Empress Wu Zetian)
nodes.role: Classical Imperial Silk Road Dynasties Connecting China to Parthia, India & Rome
nodes.notes: Han Gaozu (Liu Bang) founded the 400-year Han Dynasty; Han Wudi opened the Silk Road via Zhang Qian to Fergana/Bactria/Parthia (and court historian Sima Qian wrote the Shiji!). Tang Taizong & Wu Zetian presided over cosmopolitan Chang'an.

nodes.notes: Seven Heavenly Generations: 1. Kuni-toko-tachi, 2. Kuni-no-sa-tsuchi, 3. Toyo-kumu-nu, 4. Uhiji-ni & Suhiji-ni, 5. Oho-to-nochi & Oho-to-mahe, 6. Omo-taru & Kashiko-ne, 7. nodes.name: 1. Börte Čino ('Blue-Grey Wolf') & Qo'ai Maral ('Fallow Doe')
nodes.role: Heaven-Ordained Ancestors of the Mongol Borjigin Lineage
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Crossed the Tenggis Sea to Burqan Qaldun at the headwaters of the Onan River (Secret History of the Mongols §1, Rachewiltz p. 1).

nodes.name: 2–11. Batačiqan → Tamača → Qoričar Mergen → A'ujam Boro'ul → Sali Qača'u → Yeke Nidün → Sem Soči → Qarču → Borjigidai Mergen → Toroqoljin Bayan
nodes.role: Ten Ancestral Generations from Börte Čino to Dobun Mergen
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Borjigidai Mergen (+ Mongqoljin Qo'a) -> Toroqoljin Bayan (+ Boroqčin Qo'a), father of Du'a Soqor (Dörben clan) and Dobun Mergen.

nodes.name: 12–13. Dobun Mergen & Lady Alan Qo'a → Five Sons (Bügünütei, Belgünütei, Buqu Qatagi, Buqatu Salji & Bodončar Mungqaq)
nodes.role: The Five Arrows Parable & Founder of the Borjigin Royal Clan
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Alan Qo'a (of Qori Tumat) taught her five sons unity using the famous parable of the five arrows. Her youngest son Bodončar Mungqaq (conceived by a radiant golden light!) founded the Borjigin clan — while his stepson Jajiradai became ancestor of Genghis Khan's blood-brother & rival Jamuqa!

nodes.name: 14–18. Qabiči Ba'atur → Menen Tudun (7 Sons incl. Barulas!) → Qači Külük → Qaidu → Bai Šingqor Doqšin → Tumbinai Sečen → Qabul Qa'an (1st All-Mongol Qan!) & Ambaqai Qa'an → Bartan Ba'atur
nodes.role: Khamag Mongol Khagans & Founder of the Barlas Clan (Ancestors of Timur!)
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Menen Tudun's sons Qači'u/Qačula founded the Barulas (Barlas) clan — later ancestors of Timur (Tamerlane) and the Mughal Emperors! Qabul Qa'an became 1st Khan of All Mongols; his sons included Qutula Qa'an and Bartan Ba'atur.

nodes.name: 19. Yisügei Ba'atur & Lady Hö'elün (Olqunu'ut) → Temüjin, Qasar, Qači'un, Temüge, Temülün (+ Bekter & Belgütei)
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Yisügei Ba'atur (poisoned by Tatars when Temüjin was 9) & fierce mother Lady Hö'elün raised Temüjin (born clutching a blood clot at Deli'ün Boldaq!), brothers Joči Qasar, Qači'un, Temüge Otčigin, sister Temülün, and half-brothers Bekter & Belgütei (by Mother Sučigil).

nodes.name: 20. Temüjin / Činggis Qa'an (Genghis Khan, 1162–1227) & Empress Börte (Onggirat)
nodes.role: Founder of the Mongol Empire (Largest Contiguous Land Empire in History)
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Unified the Steppe in 1206 CE as Činggis Qa'an. With principal wife Lady Börte (plus Yisüi, Yisügen, Qulan & Ibaqa Beki) fathered the 4 Great Imperial Sons (Jöči, Ča'adai, Ögödei, Tolui) and 5 diplomat daughters (Qojin, Al Altun, Čečeyigen, Alaqa, Tümelün).

nodes.name: 21–22. The Four Great Houses: Jöči (→ Batu Khan, Golden Horde), Ča'adai (→ Büri), Ögödei Qa'an (+ Töregene → Güyük) & Tolui (+ Sorqaqtani Beki → Möngke Qa'an, Qubilai Qa'an / Kublai Khan & Hülegü Khan)
nodes.role: Great Khans of the Golden Horde, Chagatai, Yuan China & Ilkhanate Persia
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Tolui & Kereyit Christian princess Sorqaqtani Beki produced Möngke (4th Great Khan), Kublai Khan (founder of China's Yuan Dynasty, host of Marco Polo!), and Hülegü (founder of the Persian Ilkhanate). Jöči's son Batu founded the Golden Horde; Ögödei & Güyük ruled Karakorum!
